Jehovah's Witnesses don't celebrate Christmas because they believe it's a pagan tradition that was incorporated into Christianity. So, Daniel probably doesn't want to participate in that. But does that mean I should exclude him from my Christmas traditions? I don't want to make him feel left out, but I also don't want to go against my own beliefs. Maybe I should think about why I send Christmas cards in the first place. It's to share joy, express love, and celebrate the birth of Jesus. Daniel is family, and I value our connection. If I stop sending him a card, could that create a barrier or make him feel distant? On the other hand, if I do send him a card, even though he doesn't celebrate Christmas, maybe it's a way to still show him love and keep our relationship strong. It could be a way to show that I respect his beliefs while still maintaining our connection. I also need to reflect on the teachings of my faith. Christianity emphasizes love, compassion, and understanding. It's important to consider how my actions align with my faith's values. In the end, I think the key is to show love and respect, regardless of our differing beliefs.
